derivations.claim: The stated $E_i>0$ and $E_i^2-|\mathbf p_i|^2=M_i^2>0$ imply $|\mathbf v_i|<1$. For each $i$ and $\mathbf n\in S^2$, $p_i\cdot q=\omega E_i(1-\mathbf v_i\cdot\mathbf n) \ge\omega E_i(1-|\mathbf v_i|)>0$. Since there are finitely many massive terms, $K^\mu(\mathbf n)=\sum_i s_iQ_i(1,\mathbf v_i)/(1-\mathbf v_i\cdot\mathbf n)$; each denominator is bounded below by $1-|\mathbf v_i|>0$, so $K$ and its transverse components are bounded. For the measurable orthonormal frame $(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2,\mathbf n)$, $\sum_r|\mathbf K\cdot\epsilon_r|^2 =|\mathbf K-(\mathbf K\cdot\mathbf n)\mathbf n|^2=|K_\perp|^2$. Thus the integrand is nonnegative and measurable, and compactness of $S^2$ gives $0\le C<\infty$.

For the one-charge rest-to-velocity current, put $\mu=\mathbf n\cdot\hat{\mathbf z}$. Its spatial current is $\mathbf K=v\hat{\mathbf z}/(1-v\mu)$, hence $|K_\perp|^2=v^2(1-\mu^2)/(1-v\mu)^2$. Integrating over azimuth and then setting $x=1-v\mu$ gives $$I(v):=\int_{-1}^{1}\frac{v^2(1-\mu^2)}{(1-v\mu)^2}\,d\mu =\frac1v\int_{1-v}^{1+v} \left(\frac{v^2-1}{x^2}+\frac2x-1\right)dx =\frac1v\left[\frac{1-v^2}{x}+2\log x-x\right]_{1-v}^{1+v} =\frac2v\log\frac{1+v}{1-v}-4.$$ Therefore $$C(v)=\frac{g_{\mathrm{em}}^2}{2(2\pi)^3}(2\pi I(v)) =\frac{\alpha}{\pi} \left(\frac1v\log\frac{1+v}{1-v}-2\right).$$ For $f(v)=\log((1+v)/(1-v))-2v$, $f(0)=0$ and $f'(v)=2v^2/(1-v^2)>0$ on $(0,1)$, so $C(v)>0$.

The fixed-current, charge-balance, transverse-polarization, and cutoff hypotheses match [L1]. The current formula simplifies to $J(q)=K(\mathbf n)/\omega$, and step 1.1 identifies the polarization sum with $|K_\perp|^2$, exactly the angular convention of [L1]. This is a conditional use of the inspected draft carrier at its actual interface.

For each spatial direction $n$ where the prescribed real polarization frame is orthonormal, define $R_n:\mathbb C^2\to n^\perp\subset\mathbb C^3$ by $R_na=\sum_ra_r\epsilon_r(n)$. Direct expansion gives $\overline{R_na}\cdot R_nb=\sum_r\overline a_rb_r$. For every complex transverse vector $v$, its real and imaginary parts are in the real plane spanned by the two frame vectors, so $v=\sum_r(\epsilon_r\cdot v)\epsilon_r$; these coefficients give the inverse. The frame is measurable, hence $Rh(\mathbf q)=R_{\mathbf q/|\mathbf q|}h(\mathbf q)$ is a measurable unitary from $\mathfrak h_E$ onto [L1]'s $\mathbb C^3$ transverse energy space, preserving the weighted integral pairing; its inverse has components $\epsilon_r\cdot v$ and is also measurable. Composing $R$ with the unitary $U$ of [L1] gives precisely the displayed $U_E$ with its unchanged factor $\hbar c/\sqrt{(2\pi)^3 2|\mathbf k|}$. Because $J\cdot\epsilon_r=-\mathbf K\cdot\epsilon_r/\omega$, the prescribed amplitude satisfies $Rh_{\lambda,\Lambda}=-g_{\mathrm{em}}K_\perp/\omega$ on the cutoff shell. With $g>0$ from [F2], put $\sigma=-g_{\mathrm{em}}/g\in\{-1,+1\}$. Thus $U_Eh_{\lambda,\Lambda}=\sigma f_\lambda$ in [L1]'s notation, and its exact squared norm is $N_\gamma$. This sign does not change any sector norm or energy: on sector $n$ it multiplies the coherent tensor by $\sigma^n$, and this direct-sum unitary preserves the energy domain and commutes with the sector energy multipliers. Consequently [L1]'s coherent-sector and energy formulas apply to the normalized vector in this Statement. These uses require only its displayed mathematical interfaces, not its separate infrared clause.

By [F5]–[F6], $P_n$ is an orthogonal projection and $I-P_n$ is its orthogonal complement. The two Kraus operators $P_n$ and $I-P_n$ are bounded and satisfy $P_n^*P_n+(I-P_n)^*(I-P_n)=P_n+(I-P_n)=I$, so they form a normalized finite projective instrument. The state from step 3.1 is a unit vector. Put $\rho_{\lambda,\Lambda}:=T_{\Psi_{\lambda,\Lambda},\Psi_{\lambda,\Lambda}}$, with $T_{\Psi,\Psi}x=\Psi\langle\Psi,x\rangle_2$; by the unit-vector case in [A3], this is the density-operator input to the Born postulate. Applying its outcome formula to the first Kraus operator $P_n$ gives $p_n=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{\lambda,\Lambda}P_n)=\|P_n\Psi_{\lambda,\Lambda}\|^2$. This uses the finite two-outcome partition for each singleton event and assumes no countably infinite Kraus instrument.

The expected photon energy is the energy-coordinate expectation from [L1], transferred to the adopted free Hamiltonian $H_\gamma$ by its unitary map and [A2]. The cutoffs are energies in joules, so $C(\Lambda-\lambda)$ has unit joule.

Assume $C>0$ for the nonconvergence claim. The Segal–Weyl supplier [F7] requires a separable complex Hilbert space; [F8] verifies this for $\mathfrak h_T$, and $u_j\in\mathfrak h_T$ by [L1]. Let $\lambda_j=\Lambda2^{-j}$ for $j\ge1$, and set $u_j=U_Eh_{\lambda_j,\Lambda}$ and $V_j=W(-i\sqrt2u_j)$. The difference $u_{j+1}-u_j$ is the same current amplitude restricted to the shell $\lambda_{j+1}<\omega<\lambda_j$. Applying [L1]'s cutoff norm formula to that shell gives $\|u_{j+1}-u_j\|^2=C\log(\lambda_j/\lambda_{j+1})=C\log2$. The explicit exponential-vector formula in [F7] gives $\Psi_{\lambda_j,\Lambda}=V_j\Omega$ for either sign of the amplitude. Unitarity and the Weyl product law in [F7] give $V_j^*V_{j+1}=e^{i\theta_j}W(-i\sqrt2(u_{j+1}-u_j))$ for some real phase $\theta_j$. Applying the vacuum expectation formula in [F7] yields $$|\langle\Psi_{\lambda_j,\Lambda},\Psi_{\lambda_{j+1},\Lambda}\rangle_2| =e^{-\|u_{j+1}-u_j\|^2/2}=e^{-C\log2/2}<1.$$

The projection $P_n$ retains exactly sector $n$ by [F5]. The sector formula from [L1] gives $P_n\Psi_{\lambda,\Lambda} =e^{-N_\gamma/2}(U_Eh_{\lambda,\Lambda})^{\otimes_s n}/\sqrt{n!}$. The symmetric tensor norm is multiplicative and $U_E$ preserves the one-particle norm, so $p_n=e^{-N_\gamma}N_\gamma^n/n!$.

The exponential series gives $\sum_{n\ge0}p_n=e^{-N_\gamma}e^{N_\gamma}=1$ and, by reindexing its nonnegative terms, $\sum_{n\ge0}n p_n=e^{-N_\gamma}N_\gamma e^{N_\gamma}=N_\gamma$. The zero-sector term is $e^{-N_\gamma}$, including $N_\gamma=0$ under $0^0=1$.

For unit vectors $x,y$, expansion of $\|x-\zeta y\|^2$ and choice of $\zeta$ to align their inner product give $\inf_{|\zeta|=1}\|x-\zeta y\|^2=2-2|\langle x,y\rangle_2|$. Step 4.3 therefore gives the fixed positive squared adjacent-ray distance $2(1-e^{-C\log2/2})$ along $\lambda_j$. A projective-ray limit would make these adjacent distances tend to zero, a contradiction. Ordinary Fock-norm convergence is the special case without phase adjustment and is also impossible. The energy from step 4.2 tends to the finite value $C\Lambda$; nonconvergence is not caused by divergent mean energy.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
This is a conditional mathematical theorem about the prescribed current and
free coherent-state construction defined below, under the exact supplier
interfaces [F2] and [L1]. Here “soft current” is only a name for the displayed
rational function: no scattering-amplitude factorization or approximation
claim is made. The weak-zero and no-strong-limit conclusions are conditional
on [L1]; the projective-ray conclusion is proved separately in step 7.1.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the constants and conventions of
[[def-qft-example-data]], and that the two supplier interfaces [F2]
and [L1] hold exactly as stated below. Let $I$ be a finite, possibly empty,
set of leg labels. A leg $i\in I$ carries an energy $E_i>0$ in joules,
a dimensionless velocity $v_i=\mathbf v_{i,\rm phys}/c\in\mathbb R^3$ with
$\mathbf v_{i,\rm phys}$ in m s$^{-1}$ and
$|v_i|<1$, a dimensionless charge number $Q_i\in\mathbb R$ (physical charge
$eQ_i$ coulombs), and an orientation sign $\eta_i\in\{-1,1\}$, with
$\eta_i=-1$ for an incoming leg and $+1$ for an outgoing leg. Require charge
balance $\sum_{i\in I}\eta_iQ_i=0$. Use
$h=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)$ and
$h(a,b)=a^0b^0-\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b$ for algebraic four-vector
contractions. For $n\in S^2:=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=1\}$ and energy
$\omega>0$ in joules, put
$$ p_i=E_i(1,v_i),\qquad q=\omega(1,n),\qquad K:S^2\to\mathbb R^4,\quad K(n)=\sum_{i\in I}\eta_iQ_i\frac{(1,v_i)}{1-v_i\cdot n}. $$
Each $p_i$ has positive energy and
$h(p_i,p_i)=E_i^2(1-|v_i|^2)>0$; this timelike condition is the precise
meaning of “massive” here, with rest mass
$m_i=E_i\sqrt{1-|v_i|^2}/c^2>0$. The prescribed current is the function
$J(q)=\sum_{i\in I}\eta_iQ_i\,p_i/h(p_i,q)$ on
$\{\omega(1,n):\omega>0,\ n\in S^2\}$. Since
$h(p_i,q)=E_i\omega(1-v_i\cdot n)>0$, this equals $K(n)/\omega$.
Thus $K$ is dimensionless and $J(q)$ has units $\mathrm J^{-1}$.
Write $K(n)=(K^0(n),\mathbf K(n))$, let $P_T(n)=I-n\otimes n$, and
$K_\perp(n)=P_T(n)\mathbf K(n)$. Define $d\Omega$ as Euclidean chart
surface measure on $S^2$ and
$$ C=\frac{g^2}{2(2\pi)^3}\int_{S^2}|K_\perp(n)|^2\,d\Omega(n)\ge0. $$
Here $g>0$ is the dimensionless coupling of [[def-qft-example-data]] and
$\lambda,\Lambda$ are energy cutoffs in joules. Write $\mathbf q=\omega n$
for the spatial energy coordinate, distinct from the four-vector
$q=(\omega,\mathbf q)$ above. For $\mathbf q\ne0$, put $\omega=|\mathbf q|$
and $n=\mathbf q/|\mathbf q|$ and define
$$ h_\lambda(\mathbf q)=g\frac{K_\perp(n)}{\omega}\mathbf1_{\{\lambda<\omega<\Lambda\}},\qquad 0<\lambda<\Lambda; $$
Set $h_\lambda(0)=0$ and regard $h_\lambda$ as a function of $\mathbf q$.
Define
$\mathcal H_{E,T}:=\{h\in L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf q/[(2\pi)^3 2|\mathbf q|];\mathbb C^3):\mathbf q\cdot h(\mathbf q)=0\ {\rm a.e.}\}$,
with the componentwise Hermitian integral pairing linear in its second
variable. On this energy-coordinate transverse Hilbert space the exact norm is
$$ N_\lambda=\|h_\lambda\|^2=C\log(\Lambda/\lambda). $$
The energy-coordinate wavefunction has units $\mathrm J^{-1}$ and its
one-particle measure has units $\mathrm J^2$, so $N_\lambda$ and $C$ are
dimensionless; its value at $q=0$ is immaterial to this $L^2$ vector.
Under the canonical unitary $U:\mathcal H_{E,T}\to\mathcal H_T$ specified and proved in step 3.1,
the same vector is represented by the length-coordinate vector $f_\lambda$
defined as follows. Set $f_\lambda(0)=0$ and, for $k\ne0$, define
$$ f_\lambda(k)=\mathbf1_{\{\lambda/(\hbar c)<|k|<\Lambda/(\hbar c)\}} |k|^{-3/2}b(k/|k|),\qquad b(n)=\frac{gK_\perp(n)}{\sqrt{2(2\pi)^3}},\qquad \int_{S^2}|b|^2\,d\Omega=C. $$
Here $b$ is dimensionless and the $L^2(d^3k)$ wavefunction $f_\lambda$ has
units $\mathrm m^{3/2}$.
The normalized coherent vector
$\Psi_\lambda=W(-i\sqrt2 f_\lambda)\Omega
=\exp(-N_\lambda/2)\epsilon(f_\lambda)$ has squared norm in sector $m$

citations.quote: The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following statement.
Define $$\alpha=\frac{e^2}{4\pi\epsilon_0\hbar c},\qquad g=e\sqrt{\frac{\mu_0c}{\hbar}}=\sqrt{4\pi\alpha}>0.$$

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ [[def-countable-choice]]. Use the SI/natural
normalizations of [[def-qft-framework-units]] and
[[def-qft-example-data]], in particular the spacetime metric
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, the algebraic energy-momentum metric
$h=-\eta=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)$, and the dimensionless coupling
$g_{\mathrm{em}}$ with $g_{\mathrm{em}}^2=4\pi\alpha$. For a finite nonempty
index set $i=1,\ldots,m$, take rest energies $M_i>0$ in joules and energy-momentum
vectors $p_i=(E_i,\mathbf p_i)\in\mathbb R^4$ with components in joules,
$E_i>0$, and $E_i^2-|\mathbf p_i|^2=M_i^2$. The sign $E_i>0$ selects the
future mass shell in the adopted $(-,+,+,+)$ spacetime convention. Put
$\mathbf v_i=\mathbf p_i/E_i$, so $|\mathbf v_i|<1$. Choose signs
$s_i\in\{-1,+1\}$ and real dimensionless charges
$Q_i$ satisfying $\sum_i s_iQ_i=0$. These are prescribed current data, not
dynamical charged-particle trajectories.

For $\mathbf n\in S^2$, let $q=(\omega,\omega\mathbf n)$ with photon energy
$\omega>0$ in joules and define
$$p_i\cdot q:=E_i\omega-\mathbf p_i\cdot(\omega\mathbf n),\qquad J^\mu(q):=\sum_{i=1}^m s_iQ_i\frac{p_i^\mu}{p_i\cdot q},\qquad K^\mu(\mathbf n):=\omega J^\mu(\omega,\omega\mathbf n).$$
The dot in this current formula is $h$-contraction; in particular
$p_i\cdot q=\omega E_i(1-\mathbf v_i\cdot\mathbf n)>0$. Choose measurable
real orthonormal spatial polarizations $\epsilon_1(\mathbf n),\epsilon_2(\mathbf n)$
with $\mathbf n\cdot\epsilon_r(\mathbf n)=0$ almost everywhere. Put
$\epsilon_r^\mu=(0,\epsilon_r)$ and
$K\cdot\epsilon_r:=-\mathbf K\cdot\epsilon_r$. Define the finite nonnegative
angular coefficient
$$C:=\frac{g_{\mathrm{em}}^2}{2(2\pi)^3} \int_{S^2}\sum_{r=1}^{2}|K(\mathbf n)\cdot\epsilon_r(\mathbf n)|^2\,d\Omega.$$

For fixed energy cutoffs $0<\lambda<\Lambda<\infty$ in joules, define
$\mathfrak h_E=L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf q/[(2\pi)^3 2\omega];\mathbb C^2)$,
where $\omega=|\mathbf q|$, and
$$h_{\lambda,\Lambda,r}(\mathbf q) =g_{\mathrm{em}}J(q)\cdot\epsilon_r(\mathbf q/|\mathbf q|) \,\mathbf1_{\{\lambda<|\mathbf q|<\Lambda\}}.$$
The current draft mathematical supplier
[[thm-qft-example-soft-current-angular-coherent]] supplies the $\mathbb C^3$
transverse energy-space norm and unitary conversion. The measurable
orthonormal polarization frame gives the pointwise unitary identification
$h\mapsto\sum_{r=1}^2h_r\epsilon_r$ proved in step 3.1; composing it with
that conversion identifies $\mathfrak h_E$ with the positive transverse
one-particle space $\mathfrak h_T$ of [[def-qft-photon-transverse-space]]
by the unitary map below, where for $\mathbf k\ne0$ the notation
$\epsilon_r(\mathbf k)$ denotes the homogeneous extension
$\epsilon_r(\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|)$ of the supplied sphere frame:
$$(U_Eh)(\mathbf k)= \sqrt{\frac{(\hbar c)^2}{(2\pi)^3\,2|\mathbf k|}} \sum_{r=1}^{2}h_r(\hbar c\,\mathbf k)\epsilon_r(\mathbf k), \qquad \mathbf k\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}.$$
Here $\mathbf k$ is a wave vector in $\mathrm m^{-1}$ and
$\hbar c\,\mathbf k$ is the corresponding energy-momentum vector in joules.
Set $N_\gamma:=C\log(\Lambda/\lambda)$ and prepare the normalized coherent
vector in the free photon Fock space
$$\Psi_{\lambda,\Lambda} =e^{-N_\gamma/2}\bigoplus_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{(U_Eh_{\lambda,\Lambda})^{\otimes_s n}}{\sqrt{n!}} \in\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h_T),$$
where the $n=0$ term is the vacuum sector. Let $P_n$ be the number-sector
projection from [[def-qft-x03-photon-count-pvm]] and define
$p_n$ as the model probability assigned to outcome $n$ by the finite
two-outcome projective partition $\{\{n\},\mathbb R\setminus\{n\}\}$.
Then
$$p_n=e^{-N_\gamma}\frac{N_\gamma^n}{n!},\qquad n\in\mathbb N_0,$$
with $0^0:=1$; these probabilities sum to one, the mean photon count is
$N_\gamma$, and the vacuum probability is $e^{-N_\gamma}$. The expected
photon energy is
$$\langle\Psi_{\lambda,\Lambda},H_\gamma\Psi_{\lambda,\Lambda}\rangle =C(\Lambda-\lambda)\ \mathrm J,$$
for $H_\gamma=\hbar c\,d\Gamma(|\mathbf k|)$ of
[[post-qft-free-photon-model]]. If $C>0$, the family has no Fock-norm or
projective-ray limit as $\lambda\downarrow0$ (projective-ray convergence means
norm convergence after allowing a unit-modulus phase for each cutoff), although
its mean energy tends to the finite value $C\Lambda$.

For the prescribed one-charge rest-to-velocity current with final velocity
$v\hat{\mathbf z}$, $0<v<1$, take
$s_{\rm in}=-1$, $Q_{\rm in}=1$, $p_{\rm in}=(M,\mathbf0)$ and
$s_{\rm out}=+1$, $Q_{\rm out}=1$,
$p_{\rm out}=(M\gamma_v,M\gamma_v v\hat{\mathbf z})$, where $M>0$ is the
rest energy and $\gamma_v=(1-v^2)^{-1/2}$. The same coefficient is
$$C(v)=\frac{\alpha}{\pi} \left(\frac1v\log\frac{1+v}{1-v}-2\right)>0.$$
If $C>0$, the cutoff family has no Fock-norm or projective-ray limit as
$\lambda\downarrow0$; the proof below derives this from adjacent-shell
overlaps and does not use the supplier's separate conditional infrared-limit
clause. Its required norm and coherent-state inputs remain conditional on
the inspected draft supplier until its upstream inputs are current. This
prediction concerns only the constructed positive free coherent state and
its count PVM under the adopted physical assumptions. It does not infer that
a full interacting-QED scattering event emits that state or that a detector
realizes this PVM.

derivations.claim: Substituting $v=\tfrac12$ into [F2] gives $C=(\alpha/\pi)(2\log 3-2)>0$, and $\log(\Lambda/\lambda)=\log(\mathrm e)=1$. Thus the mean count is $C$, $p_0=e^{-C}$, and the general count formula specializes to $p_n=e^{-C}C^n/n!$.

Since $\lambda=\Lambda/\mathrm e$, the energy formula in [F2] gives $C(\Lambda-\lambda)=C\Lambda(1-\mathrm e^{-1})$ joules. After $j$ successive halvings, $\lambda_j=\Lambda\mathrm e^{-1}2^{-j}$, so $\log(\Lambda/\lambda_j)=1+j\log2$ and the mean count is $C(1+j\log2)$. The mean energy is $C(\Lambda-\lambda_j)\to C\Lambda$ and [F2] gives no Fock-vector or projective-ray limit when $C>0$. These remain predictions for the prescribed current and prepared free state.
